title: Our God, Where'er Thy People Meet
description: Our God, Where'er Thy People Meet in Tonic Solfa to UXBRIDGE, doh is E: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: William Cowper wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 910 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “For Social Worship”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to UXBRIDGE; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Our God, wher-e'er thy peo-ple meet, There they be-hold thy mer-cy seat; Wher-e'er they seek thee, thou art found, And ev-ery place is hal-lowed ground.

lines: Our God, where'er thy people meet,
Where'er they seek thee, thou art found,
And every place is hallowed ground.
For thou, within no walls confined,
Such ever bring thee where they come,
And, going, take thee to their home.
Here may we prove the power of prayer
To strengthen faith, and sweeten care;
To teach our faint desires to rise,
And bring all heaven before our eyes.
Lord, we are few, but thou art near;
Nor short thine arm, nor deaf thine ear:
O, rend the heavens, comes quickly down,
And make a thousand hearts thine own!

licence: Public domain: William Cowper died in 1800.
credits: Words by William Cowper (1731–1800), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to UXBRIDGE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
